articles.headline: Ryan Blaney wins Straight Talk Wireless 400 (NASCAR Cup Series Championship Race)
articles.dek: Official finish, points and how the championship looks after the race.
articles.body:
Ryan Blaney won Straight Talk Wireless 400 (NASCAR Cup Series Championship Race) at Homestead-Miami Speedway, starting P6 and leading 76 laps. Denny Hamlin finished second and Chris Buescher was third.

The race ran 200 laps with 8 cautions.

Chase Elliott was the biggest mover, gaining 30 spots from P36 to P6.

Denny Hamlin leads the championship with 1217 points, 124 ahead of Chris Buescher.
articles.author: Jamie Kowalski

posts.text: William Byron in media center after winning the 500: "We just kept our nose clean and executed when it mattered. Proud of everyone at Hendrick."
Briscoe started pole and finished P4, hell yeah what a start to the year
Briscoe choked away laps led though, total fraud watch
be so serious he led 23 laps at daytona

posts.title: Daytona 500 post-race discussion thread
posts.text: Another Byron win. Seven cautions for this parade. The cars all look identical and nobody can pass unless there is a train. Disgraceful.
aint that the truth... cars just run around in circles waiting for the big one... miss the old days when drivers actually raced each other without saving fuel
The racing is fine you guys just complain about everything. Byron drove a smart race.
Smart race? He rode around in a pack and lucked out on the last restart. Anyone can do that.
Who actually thought Byron was going to lose that after the last caution? Be honest.
poll: Thought Hocevar was taking them both

posts.text: People acting surprised when the 24 wins a superspeedway race are telling on themselves. It is not rocket science.
my bet slip had byron winning and i am not complaining at all
Daniel Suárez started P36 and finished P7 today at Daytona. Largest position gain in the field.
suarez only got up there because half the field crashed out, total fraud
from dead last to top 10 at daytona is still insane car control, chat was screaming watching him thread those gaps

posts.title: Hocevar P3 finish
posts.text: Hocevar P3! Kid can actually wheel these superspeedway cars.
He just stayed out of the wrecks by pure luck. He will wreck half the field next week.
salt is unreal. led 25 laps and finished top 3. deal with it.
New episode up! We are breaking down Byron's Daytona win and asking why Blaney and McDowell never got anything going. Who impressed you the most today?
Preece keeping his nose clean for P10 after starting way back at P33. Solid start.
Buescher P12 with zero damage and no laps led, quietly bagging points
Looking at how strategy played out today, staying out during that mid-race sequence saved a few teams' days. If you pitted when the fuel window opened you got caught behind the wrong train.
Denny drove a great race to get P2. Strategy worked out in the end.
Did anyone ask why Elliott finished a lap down in P23? Broadcast completely missed it.

posts.title: Where was the 12 car all day?
posts.text: blaney suspension issues... typical daytona luck for him... playoff format ruins any recovery when your car breaks like that
at least blaney finished before zane smith got caught in that wreck. rough day for the 91
Custer got P14 with a clean car so I am happy. Strategy kept them out of trouble.

chase.headline: Opening Standings Provide Minimal Clarity
chase.summary: With only one race in the books, our predictive models have very little data to process, keeping the early odds tightly grouped. It is far too early to overread these numbers or discuss cut lines while we are twenty-five races away from the postseason. We simply look at the points board and wait for more data.

notes.william byron: Byron sits atop the standings with fifty-five points and an early win after taking the Daytona 500.
notes.denny hamlin: Hamlin opens his campaign in second place with thirty-five points.
notes.carson hocevar: Hocevar starts strong in third position with thirty-four points.
notes.daniel suárez: Suárez holds seventh place with thirty points after charging up from thirty-sixth at Daytona.

race.headline: Heading to Atlanta for Race Two
race.summary: The Cup Series moves to EchoPark Speedway for the Autotrader 400 superspeedway showdown. Denny Hamlin leads the win odds at thirteen percent, followed by Ty Gibbs at ten percent and Chase Briscoe at nine percent. Expect high chaos with Ryan Blaney, Austin Dillon, Michael McDowell, and John Hunter Nemechek carrying the highest wreck risk at fifty-five percent.

notes.denny hamlin: Hamlin opens as the win favorite at thirteen percent on the superspeedway.
notes.ty gibbs: Gibbs sits right behind at ten percent win odds for Atlanta.
notes.william byron: Byron is expected to run well here alongside Suárez, Reddick, Logano, Buescher, and Preece.
notes.ryan blaney: Blaney shares the highest wreck risk of the weekend at fifty-five percent.

season.headline: Just One Race Down and Folks Are Already Talking
season.summary: We have run one single race out of thirty-six and people are already asking me to predict the whole year. Odds are not even open yet because it is way too early for chase talk or title favorites. Let us just watch the racing unfold instead of trying to read tea leaves in February.

notes.william byron: Byron grabbed fifty-five points and a Daytona win to kick off his year right.
notes.daniel suárez: Suárez put on a show moving from thirty-sixth to seventh at Daytona to grab thirty early points.
Stenhouse quietly grabbed thirty-one points to start the year inside the top ten.
notes.todd gilliland: Gilliland rounds out the early points list in fifteenth with twenty-two.
